title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 88–90). X is a space with a stratification by strata X_i. This structure is meant for the boundary of the compactified moduli spaces M̄_{g,ν}, where the divisor at infinity has normal crossings. On the previous page Grothendieck defined, for each r, a space D_{Δ_r} of 'non-strict local flags' (x, Σ_x) with Σ_x = {x ∈ X̄_{i_0} ⊂ … ⊂ X̄_{i_r}}. Here X̄_{i_k} means germs at x of closures of local strata (local branches), and repetitions are allowed. Each D_{Δ_r} is topologized through the projection D_{Δ_r} → X, which is a local immersion. The open part D°_{Δ_r} consists of the strict flags. Allowing non-strict flags provides degeneracies, so (D_{Δ_r}) becomes a simplicial space rather than a semi-simplicial one.

On this page he asks whether this simplicial space is the nerve of a category internal to Top. Equivalently, he asks whether the Segal map (303) D_{Δ_2} → D_{Δ_1} ×_{D_{Δ_0}} D_{Δ_1} is a homeomorphism. In concrete terms: is a germ-flag x ∈ X̄_{i_0} ⊂ X̄_{i_1} ⊂ X̄_{i_2} the same thing as two germ-flags x ∈ X̄_{i_0} ⊂ X̄_{i_1} and x ∈ X̄'_{j_0} ⊂ X̄'_{j_1} with X̄_{i_1} = X̄'_{j_0}?

He answers yes. A local stratification therefore defines a 'topological category':
- Objects: D_{Δ_0}, the space of non-strict local strata, i.e. pairs (x, germ of a stratum closure at x).
- Arrows: D_{Δ_1}, the space of flags x ∈ X̄_{i_0} ⊂ X̄_{i_1}.
- Source, target and composition are the obvious maps.

Arrows run from the deeper local stratum to a bigger one containing it in its closure. This is the 'exit' direction. The next page continues by studying the first-vertex map D_{Δ_r} → D_{Δ_0}, which is finite étale over the strict part. So the category is an étale-type topological category: each object has a finite discrete set of outgoing arrows, namely the poset of local strata containing a given local stratum.

Purpose: to encode the combinatorial-topological 'structure at infinity' (the local poset of branches of the boundary divisor, with its monodromy) as a single internal category in Top. Its nerve would then serve as a model for the boundary geometry of M̄_{g,ν} and for the tubular-neighbourhood/'dévissage' picture of the Esquisse.
errors: The equality condition should read X̄_{i_1} = X̄'_{j_0}. The transcription drops the prime; the manuscript has the prime on X'.

The homeomorphism claim is argued only at the level of germs, i.e. as a bijection. For a homeomorphism one also needs that both sides are local homeomorphisms over X, compatibly. This holds because all D_{Δ_r} → X are local immersions and the bijection commutes with the projections, but it is not spelled out. There is no substantive error.

ideas.what: Simplicial space D_{Δ_r} of non-strict local flags of germs of stratum closures, each mapping to X by a local immersion; for normal crossings these are normalizations of the multiple intersections
ideas.modern_name: semi-simplicial/simplicial normalization resolution of a normal crossings divisor; 'unzipping'/resolution of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II/III, early 1970s) for the semi-simplicial normalization; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2010s) for unzipping
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses dévissage of stratified structures and tubular neighbourhoods, but not this simplicial space explicitly

ideas.what: Segal condition D_{Δ2} ≅ D_{Δ1} ×_{D_{Δ0}} D_{Δ1}, making the stratification into a category internal to Top whose objects are local strata and whose arrows are local inclusions of strata (deeper → bigger)
ideas.modern_name: exit-path category of a stratified space (étale/discrete-fibre version); stratified space as a category internal to Top / Segal space
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s, unpublished); Treumann (2009); Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A; Segal (1968) for the nerve/Segal-condition formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck encodes a (local) stratification as a topological category. Objects are germs of strata, arrows are flags of germs in the exit direction, and composition is checked via the Segal condition on the simplicial space of flags. This is a direct ancestor of the exit-path category viewpoint on stratified spaces. Here it is formulated for the boundary of M̄_{g,ν}, which links stratified homotopy theory to the 'structure at infinity' / Teichmüller-tower programme.
missed.quote: Donc une stratification locale définit une "catégorie topologique" espace des objets = D_{Δ0} ... espace des flèches = D_{Δ1} = espace des drapeaux x∈X̄_{i0}⊂X̄_{i1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Exit-path ∞-categories and constructible sheaves on the Deligne–Mumford boundary are used in current work (e.g. stratified homotopy types of M̄_{g,n}, modular operads). This page shows Grothendieck intended this categorical encoding of the boundary as the organizing structure, probably well before MacPherson/Treumann/Lurie. It is of historical interest, and suggests studying the étale topological category itself (its classifying space and its relation to the homotopy type of the boundary) as a concrete invariant.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is natural and close to known material: Deligne's normalization resolution and exit-path categories. Seeing Grothendieck explicitly impose the Segal condition and call the stratification a topological category of local strata and flags, in the M̄_{g,ν} context, is a nice unpublished precursor. It is not a hidden theorem.
